dedupe_keys.name: noaa integrated surface database isd global hourly hourly and synoptic weather observations from more than 35 000 stations

description: The Integrated Surface Database (ISD), also called Global Hourly, is NOAA NCEI's global archive of hourly and synoptic surface weather observations in a single common ASCII format and data model. The product page read on 2026-09-26 states that ISD integrates more than 100 original sources, including records key-entered from paper forms of the 1950s to 1970s, and includes wind speed and direction, gusts, temperature, dew point, cloud, pressure, present weather, visibility, precipitation and snow depth. It draws on over 35,000 stations with some records from 1901, and more than 14,000 active stations are updated daily; the uncompressed volume is about 600 GB. Derived products include the Global Summary of the Day, Local Climatological Data and ISD-Lite, a fixed-width subset of eight common parameters. Access is free through an HTTPS archive for bulk download, the NCEI Data Access app, Climate Data Online, map viewers and web services (OGC and OPeNDAP). The page notes that NCEI is migrating to the cloud, which may delay access. No licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: station coverage and quality vary by country and period. Simulation uses are weather-driven load, heating demand and line rating models, and hazard exposure of energy assets to wind, heat and cold. Related records: data-era5-reanalysis is a gridded alternative.
